name: Owain Glyndŵr
credit: No confirmed portrait sourced for this archive.
bio: Owain Glyndŵr (c. 1354–1416), Prince of Wales, led the Welsh revolt against English rule from 1400. He was the patron of the poet Iolo Goch, who celebrated his house at Sycharth.
The quatrain here is attributed to him in Borrow's source, as translated in Welsh Poems and Ballads (1915); the attribution is traditional and uncertain.

poems.title: David Gam
poems.author: Owain Glyndŵr
poems.note: From "Wild Wales". Printed as "Attributed to Owain Glyndower"; the attribution is the source's.
poems.translator: trans. George Borrow (Welsh Poems and Ballads, 1915)
poems.text:
Shouldst thou a little red man descry
   Asking about his dwelling fair,
Tell him it under the bank doth lie,
   And its brow the mark of the coal doth bear.
